page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance features 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with 2 threads per core, operating on a burstable CPU allocation model under the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz (4.0 GB per core) and cache sizes of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3. Advanced instruction sets supported include AVX-512, AMX tile and int8, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, lacks local NVMe SSD storage, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2060.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.93 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% performance tier. Geekbench text processing also scores strongly at 2658.0. Multi-core performance falls in the middle 50% category, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7592.92, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7912.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 13934.37. Potentially uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 51.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 49.46 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput measures 14.33 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations execute at 10.25 million operations per second.

A notable architectural tradeoff is the burstable CPU allocation model alongside the complete absence of local storage. High-throughput compute tasks requiring sustained 100% CPU utilization may face performance throttling once burst credits are exhausted. Additionally, text generation speed for medium 7B parameter LLM models yields a weak rating of 7.62 tokens/sec, reflecting execution constraints on larger models. However, the presence of AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets offers qualitative compute efficiency for entry-level workloads and small LLM prompt processing (56.4 tokens/sec on 7B models) without requiring specialized hardware accelerators.

Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is suited for general-purpose application hosting, web serving, text processing, microservices, software compilation, and moderate database operations where burstable vCPU profiles align with operational patterns.
